title: From constraint models to playable puzzle games
excerpt: I wanted to play some puzzles produced by my constraint-programming experiments. That small wish grew into nine games.
content_html:
For my paper Scaling Sudoku as a Constraint Problem, I generated a repository of 434,201 Sudoku instances at five sizes between 6×6 and 36×36. I used them in constraint-programming experiments to ask which propagation scheme solves a puzzle without branching, how that changes with size, and how many clues move an instance from one hardness category to another.

I also wanted to play a few of them.

That small wish grew sideways. I now have playable versions of Sudoku, Nonogram, Queens, Zip, Loopy, Tents, Patches, Wend, and its Swedish sibling Swend. They are collected on a games page.

Each game section below includes a small model written in MiniZinc, a constraint-modelling language, and explains one part of the corresponding generator. The models are explanatory sketches rather than the programs that build the packs. Most generation and solving code uses Gecode 6.4.0. Additional programs handle importing, rasterisation, exact cover, and pack assembly.

What all nine games have in common is that I start with a solution or source image. I then add, move, or remove information until the intended answer is unique, or discard a candidate that cannot be repaired cleanly. Some of the same deductions later classify difficulty and provide hints.

Generation and uniqueness checking happen offline. The browser receives static puzzles and stored solutions; it does not run a solver. Difficulty labels come from propagation, search, or deterministic deduction measurements. They provide a relative, mechanically derived ordering within each pack; they do not estimate how difficult players will find the puzzles.

The listings were checked with MiniZinc 2.10.0. To keep them focused, they leave out input validation, search annotations, and the outer loop that rejects a candidate when a second solution exists. Output is omitted except where it defines which decisions constitute a puzzle solution.

Sudoku: from corpus to game#

The Scaling Sudoku corpus begins with 32,000 uniquely solvable base puzzles at sizes 6×6, 9×9, 16×16, 25×25, and 36×36. A generator first creates a complete grid, then removes clues while preserving uniqueness. Gecode classifies the resulting puzzles.

The classification extends the setup in Helmut Simonis’s 2005 paper Sudoku as a Constraint Problem. It tries an ordered family of propagation configurations. Val, Bnd, and Dom refer to value, bounds, and domain propagation; BS and DS add bounds or domain shaving.1 The weakest successful configuration becomes the puzzle’s hardness tag. If none finishes without branching, the tag is Search.

The basic Sudoku model is pleasantly short. The box dimensions are data, which lets the same model handle 6×6 boards with 2×3 boxes and the usual 9×9 boards with 3×3 boxes.

The playable pack is a reproducible, fixed-seed sample of 500 base puzzles from a pinned corpus revision, limited to 6×6 and 9×9 boards. An offline importer turns the selected puzzles and their known solutions into a static pack.

Making Sudoku look more like Sudoku#

Generated puzzles do not automatically have the visual symmetry people tend to expect from a published Sudoku. I did not want to generate a separate collection merely for presentation, so I wrote an offline symmetrification pass for the selected puzzles.

There are two useful freedoms. First, rows and columns can be permuted in ways that preserve the box structure: rows within a band, columns within a stack, and the bands and stacks themselves. Second, a missing rotational partner can be filled with the value from the known solution. The latter only adds information, so it cannot introduce a second solution, but it may make the puzzle easier according to the propagation classifier.

For each puzzle, the optimiser enumerates the distinct rotational pairings obtainable from box-preserving layouts and ranks them by how many clues would be needed for 180-degree rotational symmetry. It evaluates the three best-ranked layouts, first trying to complete the symmetry for each one. If that changes the hardness tag, it adds partner clues individually and keeps only additions for which Gecode reproduces the original tag. Finally, it chooses the resulting layout with the fewest asymmetric cells.

The pass made 228 of the 500 puzzles exactly rotationally symmetric and reduced the total number of asymmetric cells from 6,172 to 1,928.

Nonogram: back to regular#

In a Nonogram, the player fills cells so that the runs in every row and column match the given clues. The game also loops back to my early Gecode work. In 2005, I wrote the original Gecode nonogram example using Gilles Pesant’s regular constraint. Its model describes a line with runs of lengths a, b, ..., z by the regular expression

0* 1^a 0+ 1^b 0+ ... 0+ 1^z 0*

where 1 is a filled square and 0 is an empty one. Gecode turns the expression into a finite-state machine and constrains every row and column to follow it. The Gecode 6.4.0 example still uses the same compact idea.

Jan Wolter later included the example in his extensive survey of Paint-by-Number solvers. His assessment was rather nice: this small demonstration model performed surprisingly well alongside much larger, specialised solvers.

The MiniZinc model builds and applies the same automata directly. Its run clues are lists, so rows and columns can contain different numbers of runs without padding. The function line_regexp builds a regular-expression string from each list. MiniZinc compiles that string to a finite-state machine, and regular applies it to a row or column.

A newer icon pack starts with SVGs from the pinned Heroicons 2.2.0 and Phosphor Icons 2.1.1 archives. An offline rasteriser renders each icon at high resolution, fits it to one of four board sizes, and thresholds the result into filled and empty cells.

Each source icon is assigned to one board size, so the same image cannot reappear at several resolutions. The selector rejects rasters with extreme fill ratios, too many connected components, duplicate fingerprints, or badly balanced clues, then favours reviewed or more detailed silhouettes. The imported bitmap must satisfy the derived clues, and Gecode must find no second solution.

A deterministic replay records the initial line ambiguity and largest initial candidate set, then measures deduction rounds and unresolved cells. Together with Gecode’s search nodes and failures, these measurements rank the valid instances within each size.

Queens: grow regions around a solution#

Queens is the one-star form of Star Battle: place one queen in every row, column, and coloured region, with no two queens touching. The generator starts with a valid no-touch queen permutation and grows one orthogonally connected region from each queen. It then perturbs non-queen cells along region boundaries while preserving connectivity.

The small example below starts with the base solution and then shows the proposed region boundaries grown around it. A second solution would be valid with those boundaries, making this an invalid puzzle instance. Moving the cell marked M into the neighbouring region removes that alternative, so one boundary-cell move makes the intended solution unique. The real generator repeats this sort of change while checking region connectivity and stopping each solution count at two.

One variable per row is enough for the puzzle model. Its value is the queen’s column. Distinct columns handle the column rule, while indexing the region matrix at each queen position handles all coloured regions at once.

Region relabellings and the eight rotations and reflections of a square board are reduced to one canonical fingerprint, preventing disguised copies of the same puzzle. The generator also limits tiny and dominant regions; I chose those limits after measuring published LinkedIn Queens boards. Difficulty uses the same propagation and shaving configurations as Scaling Sudoku, followed by Search when none solves the board without branching.

Zip: ask for a counterexample#

In Zip, the player draws one path through every cell while visiting numbered clues in order and avoiding hedges. The generator represents the path as a Gecode circuit: each board cell has a successor, and an extra return node connects the final clue back to clue 1. The circuit constraint rules out disconnected subtours, while inverse path and position views make the numbered ordering constraints explicit.

The model expresses orthogonal movement with row and column offsets. For each cell, it tries the four directions. MiniZinc’s default <> turns an out-of-bounds lookup into an absent cell; since an absent cell cannot equal the successor, directions outside the board disappear from the disjunction. This avoids a separate adjacency matrix.

To decide which numbers and hedges to show, the Zip generator begins with only the first and last numbers. It asks the solver for a second path, then studies that counterexample. The example below starts after one checkpoint has already been added. Both paths obey the visible clues 1, 2, and 3.

The added clue says that the middle-left cell must occur after the top-middle one. That is true of the intended path, but not of the counterexample, so one ambiguity has disappeared. The generator repeats this: whenever possible it adds a numbered checkpoint whose position distinguishes the intended path from the alternative. Sometimes a pair of numbers is needed because the two paths visit those cells in opposite orders. A hedge is added only when numbers cannot separate the counterexample within the clue-density limit.

The process repeats until the intended path is the only solution. Number and hedge limits keep the board from filling with annotations.

Zip tries the same nine propagation and shaving configurations as Scaling Sudoku, followed by Search when none solves without branching. The interface maps the ten internal tags to relative labels from Gentle through Expert.

Loopy: hide clues from a finished loop#

Loopy is played on the edges of a square grid. The aim is to draw one closed loop without branches or crossings. A number inside a cell tells how many of its four edges belong to the loop; a blank cell imposes no such count.

The generator begins with the loop. It grows a connected patch of cells while keeping the cells outside the patch connected as well, then rejects any boundary that is not one simple loop. Once that shape is fixed, the generator counts the four surrounding loop edges for every cell and obtains a fully clued puzzle.

The MiniZinc model assigns one successor variable to each grid vertex. A vertex outside the loop points to itself. The remaining successors form one directed cycle, which is exactly the structure captured by subcircuit. An undirected grid edge belongs to the loop when either endpoint chooses the other as its successor.

The additional edge constraint rules out a directed two-cycle between adjacent vertices, which would otherwise collapse to a single undirected edge rather than a loop. The output records only in_loop, and the omitted uniqueness loop blocks each discovered edge set. It therefore treats the two directed orientations as the same puzzle solution.

The fully clued board is a useful starting point but a poor puzzle. The generator therefore tries hiding clues one at a time. A clue stays hidden only if the intended loop remains unique. For an Easy or Medium candidate, the local deduction engine also keeps the puzzle within the requested band as clues disappear.

Difficulty is measured by replaying two families of local deductions. A satisfied clue excludes its remaining edges, while a clue that needs every undecided edge forces all of them into the loop. At a grid vertex, two loop edges exclude the other incident edges; one loop edge with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge into the loop; and no selected loop edges with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge out. The bands record how many deduction rounds are needed; every selected puzzle can be completed by these rules without search.

Tents: move the trees against an alternative#

In Tents, the player places one orthogonally adjacent tent for each tree. No two tents may touch, even diagonally, and the row and column clues give the number of tents in each line. The generator starts from those tents, assigns each one a distinct orthogonally adjacent tree, and derives the counts. Those clues often admit another tent set.

The useful counterexample is the alternative set together with its possible tree matching. When the intended answer is not unique, the generator moves one tree to another square beside its intended tent, choosing a square that prevents the alternative tents from matching every tree. The tent set and line counts stay fixed. The generator recounts solutions after each move and stops when only the intended tent set remains. In the example below, dashed lines show one matching between trees and tents; M marks the moved tree.

The MiniZinc sketch does not need a decision variable for every board cell. A Coordinate record keeps a row and column together, and every tree owns one such decision record for its tent. Whole-array field projections such as tents.row then let global_cardinality count the chosen rows and columns directly. The rest of the listing uses optional lookups at board edges, imaginary 2×2 squares to enforce tent spacing, and sorted output to identify a solution by its tent set rather than a particular tree-to-tent matching.

The parameter array cell_id is only a coordinate lookup. The adjacency constraint uses the same default <> boundary idiom as Zip. Strict equality cannot match the absent value returned outside the board, so the four offsets need no edge cases.

diffn normally keeps rectangles from overlapping. Here each tent is the anchor of an imaginary 2×2 square. Two such squares overlap exactly when their anchor cells coincide or touch along an edge or corner, so one global replaces the eight-neighbour decomposition. It also implies that the tent cells are distinct. The explicit all_different is logically redundant, but it keeps the one-to-one matching visible to a dedicated matching propagator. The imaginary squares may extend past the board; without a container constraint, diffn only constrains them relative to each other.

The sorted output is deliberate. Since tents is indexed by tree, one tent set can admit several tree-to-tent matchings. The omitted uniqueness loop blocks the sorted cell identifiers, so it counts player-visible tent sets rather than matching witnesses. The native generator uses the same identity when it asks whether a second solution exists.

The player-facing Easy, Medium, and Hard labels come from replaying the deterministic deductions used by the hint engine. Easy puzzles need line-count and tent-spacing deductions, grass marks for cells without an adjacent tree, and trees with a single remaining position. Medium puzzles add locked tree sets and one-to-one matching deductions. Hard puzzles require a short failed assumption: try a tent or grass mark, propagate, and reject the assumption when it reaches a contradiction.

Empty lines are useful clues, but too many produce striped boards with large inactive areas. The generator therefore sets separate limits on empty rows and empty columns.

Patches: remove information from a tiling#

Patches asks the player to divide the board into rectangles, one per coloured clue, while respecting any given area or shape. The generator starts from a complete tiling. A bounded depth-first search tiles a square board with rectangles of area at least two, then places one clue in a corner of each rectangle. Initially, every clue gives both the rectangle’s area and its shape: square, wide, or tall.

That fully described tiling is usually too easy. The generator shuffles the clue fields and tries removing an area or shape. After every removal, an exact-cover solver counts rectangle tilings up to two; the field stays absent only when the puzzle remains unique.

The corresponding model uses one record for each clue and another for the placement variables of its rectangle. The Boolean covers view is redundant, but it expresses the exact-cover constraint clearly and gives useful propagation from cells back to rectangles. Corner placement is a convention for the generated answer, not a player rule: an alternative rectangle only has to contain its clue.

Patches classifies difficulty by giving each clue a domain of candidate rectangles. It uses three custom propagation tiers, named Val, Bnd, and Dom to match the other games. Val removes rectangles that overlap an assigned patch. Bnd also uses cell coverage: if only one clue can still cover a cell, that clue’s domain is restricted accordingly. Dom adds a local support check for the remaining uncovered cells. Bounds- and domain-shaving variants complete the set, followed by Search.

Wend and Swend: fill a path cover with words#

Wend and its Swedish sibling Swend ask the player to divide the letter grid into words of the given lengths. Every open cell belongs to one orthogonally connected word path. The two games use the same path and exact-cover models with language-specific word tables.

Generation runs that process backwards. It chooses a symmetric block mask and a path through every open cell, cuts the path into lengths between three and ten, and fills the pieces with words.

The first MiniZinc sketch models the geometric part of generation directly. The open cells are nodes in an undirected grid graph. Requiring MiniZinc’s path constraint to include every open node gives one Hamiltonian path from start to finish.

The optional board values describe both the cell identities and the graph boundary. A block contains <>, and the default <> expression gives an out-of-range lookup the same absent value. The occurs tests therefore reject both blocks and positions beyond the board. Only rightward and downward offsets are needed because path treats the edges as undirected.

path returns selected edges rather than an ordered cell array. Walking those edges from start to finish recovers the sequence. The native generator constructs that sequence directly, cuts it into the required lengths, may reverse and reorder the pieces, and fills them with words.

The published 5×5 instance below shows those three steps directly.

Those chosen words do not by themselves make a valid puzzle. The same letters may form other dictionary words, and those candidates may admit a second path cover. A trie finds every dictionary word that can be traced without reusing a cell; the second model checks whether those candidate paths have another exact cover. Every cell must occur once, and the selected paths must have the advertised lengths.

The Gecode checker stops after finding two covers and accepts only a unique decomposition.

Swend’s lexicon starts from SAOL 14 and keeps words supported by the Swedish Kelly list or NyLLex, together with reviewed additions. Wend instead uses a filtered, pinned version of the English Speller Database. Both importers remove palindromes and reversal pairs because a path can be read in either direction.

Generated boards must contain turns and straight segments, use all four directions, and survive deduplication under rotations and reflections. Within each board size, the generator ranks them by the number of traceable dictionary candidates, followed by Gecode search nodes and failures. The lower, middle, and upper thirds receive the relative labels Easy, Medium, and Hard. Within each third, the generator favours boards with more mirrored letter pairs and a balanced selection of block masks.

Hints as small propagation systems#

Some of the local deductions used to classify generated puzzles can also explain the next move to a player. Once a puzzle has a known solution, the easiest hint system is still to reveal part of it. I wanted the hint button to make a deduction when the current state supports one, and to be explicit when it falls back to a reveal.

Sudoku and Queens have explainable hints backed by a small, puzzle-neutral deduction engine. It knows about exact-one groups, capacity-one groups, conflicts, Hall sets,2 and failed-literal reasoning, which uses the same assumption-propagation-failure test as shaving. It runs rules in teaching order and keeps a shown hint active until its target has been handled. The game adapters give those ideas their concrete meaning: cells and values for Sudoku; rows, columns, regions, and attacks for Queens.

Sudoku first reports an incorrect entry. It then tries naked singles, a value with only one place in a row, column, or box, Hall sets of up to four cells,2 and finally a small negative-reasoning step: assume a candidate, propagate forced placements, and reject it if propagation reaches a conflict. Only when none of those rules applies does it reveal a value from the stored solution.

Queens follows a similar teaching order. It reports attacking or incorrect queens and a cross that hides a solution square. It marks cells directly attacked by placed queens, finds rows, columns, or regions with one candidate left, and uses locked sets when a collection of regions is confined to the same number of rows or columns. Failed-literal reasoning handles the remaining case by tentatively placing a queen and propagating until two forced queens attack or some group loses its last candidate.

The first two examples below are direct deductions. A marks squares that the deduction allows the player to cross out. In the locked-set example, R marks the candidates that justify those actions.

Nonogram uses the same line model for solving and for hints, but keeps the hint implementation local. It first reports a marked square that conflicts with the stored picture. Otherwise it enumerates all line patterns compatible with the current marks and the run clues. If every remaining pattern for a row or column agrees on an unknown square, that square is forced. Only when no line has such a deduction does the hint reveal a square from the stored solution.

The other games use narrower hint finders. Patches recomputes live rectangle domains, and Tents replays its line, matching, and failed-assumption deductions. Loopy reasons about clue saturation, vertex degree, and premature closed subloops. Zip identifies the first wrong turn or continues the known path, while Wend and Swend progressively reveal a word. When no deduction applies, the hint says that it is revealing part of the stored solution.

That keeps the distinction visible: a deduction follows from the current state, while a reveal merely helps the player resume.

Summary#

Across these games, constraints do three related jobs. They describe valid solutions, detect alternatives during generation, and support deductions for hints. The generators use uniqueness in different ways: Nonogram retains source images that pass a uniqueness check; Sudoku, Loopy, and Patches remove information while preserving a unique answer; Queens, Zip, and Tents repair counterexamples; Wend and Swend reject alternative covers.

I started with a large Sudoku corpus and wanted to play a few instances. I ended up with nine playable games (so far).

Footnotes#

  1. Shaving temporarily assigns a value and propagates to a fixpoint. If that assumption fails, the value can be removed without committing to a branch. Bounds shaving tests the current smallest and largest values of a domain; domain shaving tests every remaining value. I described the corresponding MiniZinc preprocessing modes in the LinkedIn Queens benchmarking post. ↩

  2. Hall’s theorem gives the matching condition behind all_different: any set of k variables must collectively have at least k possible values. If it has exactly k, those values are reserved for those variables and can be removed from every other domain; fewer than k proves failure. Régin’s matching-based propagator uses the general form of this argument to establish domain consistency. Puget’s bounds propagator looks for the cheaper restricted form given by Hall intervals. ↩ ↩2

This avoids a separate adjacency matrix. include "globals.mzn";int: rows;int: columns;int: cells = rows * columns;set of int: Rows = 1..rows;set of int: Columns = 1..columns;set of int: Cells = 1..cells;set of int: Nodes = 1..cells + 1;int: return_node = cells + 1;enum Directions = {Up, Right, Down, Left};array[Directions] of int: row_offset = [-1, 0, 1, 0];array[Directions] of int: column_offset = [0, 1, 0, -1];array[Rows, Columns] of Cells: board = array2d(Rows, Columns, [cell | cell in Cells]);array[Cells, Cells] of bool: hedge; % Symmetricint: number_count;array[1..number_count] of Cells: numbered_cell;array[Nodes] of var Nodes: successor;array[Cells] of var Cells: path;array[Cells] of var Cells: position;constraint circuit(successor);constraint inverse(path, position);constraint successor[return_node] = numbered_cell[1];constraint successor[numbered_cell[number_count]] = return_node;constraint forall ( row in Rows, column in Columns where board[row,column] != numbered_cell[number_count]) ( let {Cells: cell = board[row,column]} in exists (direction in Directions) ( successor[cell] = (board[ row + row_offset[direction], column + column_offset[direction] ] default <>) ) /\ not hedge[cell,successor[cell]]);constraint path[1] = numbered_cell[1];constraint path[cells] = numbered_cell[number_count];constraint forall (step in 1..cells-1) ( successor[path[step]] = path[step+1]);constraint forall (number in 1..number_count-1) ( position[numbered_cell[number]] < position[numbered_cell[number+1]]);solve satisfy; To decide which numbers and hedges to show, the Zip generator begins with only the first and last numbers. It asks the solver for a second path, then studies that counterexample. The example below starts after one checkpoint has already been added. Both paths obey the visible clues 1, 2, and 3. The added clue says that the middle-left cell must occur after the top-middle one. That is true of the intended path, but not of the counterexample, so one ambiguity has disappeared. The generator repeats this: whenever possible it adds a numbered checkpoint whose position distinguishes the intended path from the alternative. Sometimes a pair of numbers is needed because the two paths visit those cells in opposite orders. A hedge is added only when numbers cannot separate the counterexample within the clue-density limit. The process repeats until the intended path is the only solution. Number and hedge limits keep the board from filling with annotations. Zip tries the same nine propagation and shaving configurations as Scaling Sudoku, followed by Search when none solves without branching. The interface maps the ten internal tags to relative labels from Gentle through Expert. Loopy: hide clues from a finished loop# Most of a 5×5 Loopy loop Loopy is played on the edges of a square grid. The aim is to draw one closed loop without branches or crossings. A number inside a cell tells how many of its four edges belong to the loop; a blank cell imposes no such count. The generator begins with the loop. It grows a connected patch of cells while keeping the cells outside the patch connected as well, then rejects any boundary that is not one simple loop. Once that shape is fixed, the generator counts the four surrounding loop edges for every cell and obtains a fully clued puzzle. The MiniZinc model assigns one successor variable to each grid vertex. A vertex outside the loop points to itself. The remaining successors form one directed cycle, which is exactly the structure captured by subcircuit. An undirected grid edge belongs to the loop when either endpoint chooses the other as its successor. include "subcircuit.mzn";enum Cells;enum Vertices;enum Edges;enum Sides = {North, East, South, West};array[Cells] of opt 0..3: clue;array[Cells, Sides] of Edges: cell_edge;array[Edges] of Vertices: edge_from;array[Edges] of Vertices: edge_to;array[Vertices] of set of Vertices: neighbour = [ {edge_to[edge] | edge in Edges where edge_from[edge] = vertex} union {edge_from[edge] | edge in Edges where edge_to[edge] = vertex} | vertex in Vertices];array[Vertices] of var Vertices: successor;constraint forall (vertex in Vertices) ( successor[vertex] = vertex \/ successor[vertex] in neighbour[vertex]);constraint subcircuit(successor);constraint exists (vertex in Vertices) ( successor[vertex] != vertex);% An undirected edge cannot be traversed in both directions.constraint forall (edge in Edges) ( not ( successor[edge_from[edge]] = edge_to[edge] /\ successor[edge_to[edge]] = edge_from[edge] ));array[Edges] of var bool: in_loop = [ successor[edge_from[edge]] = edge_to[edge] \/ successor[edge_to[edge]] = edge_from[edge] | edge in Edges];constraint forall (cell in Cells where occurs(clue[cell])) ( sum (side in Sides) (in_loop[cell_edge[cell, side]]) = deopt(clue[cell]));solve satisfy;% Puzzle solutions are undirected edge sets, not cycle orientations.output [show(in_loop)]; The additional edge constraint rules out a directed two-cycle between adjacent vertices, which would otherwise collapse to a single undirected edge rather than a loop. The output records only in_loop, and the omitted uniqueness loop blocks each discovered edge set. It therefore treats the two directed orientations as the same puzzle solution. The fully clued board is a useful starting point but a poor puzzle. The generator therefore tries hiding clues one at a time. A clue stays hidden only if the intended loop remains unique. For an Easy or Medium candidate, the local deduction engine also keeps the puzzle within the requested band as clues disappear. Difficulty is measured by replaying two families of local deductions. A satisfied clue excludes its remaining edges, while a clue that needs every undecided edge forces all of them into the loop. At a grid vertex, two loop edges exclude the other incident edges; one loop edge with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge into the loop; and no selected loop edges with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge out. The bands record how many deduction rounds are needed; every selected puzzle can be completed by these rules without search. Tents: move the trees against an alternative# In Tents, the player places one orthogonally adjacent tent for each tree. No two tents may touch, even diagonally, and the row and column clues give the number of tents in each line. The generator starts from those tents, assigns each one a distinct orthogonally adjacent tree, and derives the counts. Those clues often admit another tent set. The useful counterexample is the alternative set together with its possible tree matching. When the intended answer is not unique, the generator moves one tree to another square beside its intended tent, choosing a square that prevents the alternative tents from matching every tree. The tent set and line counts stay fixed. The generator recounts solutions after each move and stops when only the intended tent set remains. In the example below, dashed lines show one matching between trees and tents; M marks the moved tree. The MiniZinc sketch does not need a decision variable for every board cell. A Coordinate record keeps a row and column together, and every tree owns one such decision record for its tent. Whole-array field projections such as tents.row then let global_cardinality count the chosen rows and columns directly. The rest of the listing uses optional lookups at board edges, imaginary 2×2 squares to enforce tent spacing, and sorted output to identify a solution by its tent set rather than a particular tree-to-tent matching. include "globals.mzn";int: rows;int: columns;set of int: Rows = 1..rows;set of int: Columns = 1..columns;set of int: Cells = 1..(rows * columns);enum Trees;type Coordinate = record(Rows: row, Columns: column);array[Trees] of Coordinate: trees;array[Rows] of 0..columns: row_count;array[Columns] of 0..rows: column_count;array[Rows, Columns] of Cells: cell_id = array2d(Rows, Columns, [cell | cell in Cells]);array[Trees] of var Coordinate: tents;array[Trees] of var Cells: tent_cells = [ cell_id[tents[tree].row, tents[tree].column] | tree in Trees];% Each tree chooses an orthogonally adjacent cell that is not a tree.constraint forall (tree in Trees) ( not (tents[tree] in trees) /\ exists ( row_offset, column_offset in -1..1 where abs(row_offset) + abs(column_offset) = 1 ) ( tent_cells[tree] = (cell_id[ trees[tree].row + row_offset, trees[tree].column + column_offset ] default <>) ));% diffn also makes the cells distinct, but the explicit all_different% gives the tree-to-tent matching its own Hall-style propagator.constraint all_different(tent_cells);% Count the tent rows and columns directly.constraint global_cardinality( tents.row, [row: row | row in Rows], row_count);constraint global_cardinality( tents.column, [column: column | column in Columns], column_count);% Two 2 by 2 squares overlap exactly when their anchor cells touch.constraint diffn( tents.row, tents.column, [tree: 2 | tree in Trees], [tree: 2 | tree in Trees]);solve satisfy;% Puzzle solutions are tent sets, not particular tree/tent matchings.output [show(sort(tent_cells))]; The parameter array cell_id is only a coordinate lookup. The adjacency constraint uses the same default <> boundary idiom as Zip. Strict equality cannot match the absent value returned outside the board, so the four offsets need no edge cases. diffn normally keeps rectangles from overlapping. Here each tent is the anchor of an imaginary 2×2 square. Two such squares overlap exactly when their anchor cells coincide or touch along an edge or corner, so one global replaces the eight-neighbour decomposition. It also implies that the tent cells are distinct. The explicit all_different is logically redundant, but it keeps the one-to-one matching visible to a dedicated matching propagator. The imaginary squares may extend past the board; without a container constraint, diffn only constrains them relative to each other. The sorted output is deliberate. Since tents is indexed by tree, one tent set can admit several tree-to-tent matchings. The omitted uniqueness loop blocks the sorted cell identifiers, so it counts player-visible tent sets rather than matching witnesses. The native generator uses the same identity when it asks whether a second solution exists. The player-facing Easy, Medium, and Hard labels come from replaying the deterministic deductions used by the hint engine. Easy puzzles need line-count and tent-spacing deductions, grass marks for cells without an adjacent tree, and trees with a single remaining position. Medium puzzles add locked tree sets and one-to-one matching deductions. Hard puzzles require a short failed assumption: try a tent or grass mark, propagate, and reject the assumption when it reaches a contradiction. Empty lines are useful clues, but too many produce striped boards with large inactive areas. The generator therefore sets separate limits on empty rows and empty columns. Patches: remove information from a tiling# Two patches placed on a 5×5 board Patches asks the player to divide the board into rectangles, one per coloured clue, while respecting any given area or shape. The generator starts from a complete tiling. A bounded depth-first search tiles a square board with rectangles of area at least two, then places one clue in a corner of each rectangle. Initially, every clue gives both the rectangle’s area and its shape: square, wide, or tall. That fully described tiling is usually too easy. The generator shuffles the clue fields and tries removing an area or shape. After every removal, an exact-cover solver counts rectangle tilings up to two; the field stays absent only when the puzzle remains unique. The corresponding model uses one record for each clue and another for the placement variables of its rectangle. The Boolean covers view is redundant, but it expresses the exact-cover constraint clearly and gives useful propagation from cells back to rectangles. Corner placement is a convention for the generated answer, not a player rule: an alternative rectangle only has to contain its clue. enum Shapes = {Unspecified, Square, Wide, Tall};int: rows;int: columns;set of int: Rows = 1..rows;set of int: Columns = 1..columns;int: patch_count;set of int: Patches = 1..patch_count;type PatchClue = record( Rows: row, Columns: column, 0..rows*columns: area, % 0 means absent Shapes: shape);array[Patches] of PatchClue: clue;type PatchPlacement = record( var Rows: top, var Columns: left, var 1..rows: height, var 1..columns: width);array[Patches] of PatchPlacement: placement;array[Patches, Rows, Columns] of var bool: covers;constraint forall (patch in Patches) ( placement[patch].top + placement[patch].height - 1 <= rows /\ placement[patch].left + placement[patch].width - 1 <= columns /\ placement[patch].width * placement[patch].height >= 2);constraint forall (patch in Patches, row in Rows, column in Columns) ( covers[patch,row,column] <-> row >= placement[patch].top /\ row < placement[patch].top + placement[patch].height /\ column >= placement[patch].left /\ column < placement[patch].left + placement[patch].width);constraint forall (patch in Patches) ( covers[patch,clue[patch].row,clue[patch].column]);constraint forall (patch, other in Patches where patch != other) ( not covers[patch,clue[other].row,clue[other].column]);constraint forall (row in Rows, column in Columns) ( sum (patch in Patches) (covers[patch,row,column]) = 1);constraint forall (patch in Patches where clue[patch].area > 0) ( placement[patch].width * placement[patch].height = clue[patch].area);constraint forall (patch in Patches) ( clue[patch].shape = Unspecified \/ (clue[patch].shape = Square /\ placement[patch].width = placement[patch].height) \/ (clue[patch].shape = Wide /\ placement[patch].width > placement[patch].height) \/ (clue[patch].shape = Tall /\ placement[patch].width < placement[patch].height));solve satisfy; Patches classifies difficulty by giving each clue a domain of candidate rectangles. It uses three custom propagation tiers, named Val, Bnd, and Dom to match the other games. Val removes rectangles that overlap an assigned patch. Bnd also uses cell coverage: if only one clue can still cover a cell, that clue’s domain is restricted accordingly. Dom adds a local support check for the remaining uncovered cells. Bounds- and domain-shaving variants complete the set, followed by Search. Wend and Swend: fill a path cover with words# Tracing HERBS in Wend Wend and its Swedish sibling Swend ask the player to divide the letter grid into words of the given lengths. Every open cell belongs to one orthogonally connected word path. The two games use the same path and exact-cover models with language-specific word tables. Generation runs that process backwards. It chooses a symmetric block mask and a path through every open cell, cuts the path into lengths between three and ten, and fills the pieces with words. The first MiniZinc sketch models the geometric part of generation directly. The open cells are nodes in an undirected grid graph. Requiring MiniZinc’s path constraint to include every open node gives one Hamiltonian path from start to finish. include "globals.mzn";int: rows;int: columns;set of int: Rows = 1..rows;set of int: Columns = 1..columns;enum Cells;array[Rows, Columns] of opt Cells: board; % <> marks a blocktype Offset = record(int: row, int: column);array[1..2] of Offset: forward = [ (row: 0, column: 1), (row: 1, column: 0),];function opt Cells: neighbour(Rows: row, Columns: column, Offset: offset) = board[ row + offset.row, column + offset.column ] default <>;type Edge = record(Cells: from, Cells: to);array[int] of Edge: edge = [ ( from: deopt(board[row,column]), to: deopt(neighbour(row, column, offset)) ) | row in Rows, column in Columns, offset in forward where occurs(board[row,column]) /\ occurs(neighbour(row, column, offset))];set of int: Edges = index_set(edge);var Cells: start;var Cells: finish;array[Edges] of var bool: used_edge;constraint path( from: edge.from, to: edge.to, source: start, sink: finish, ns: [cell: true | cell in Cells], es: used_edge);% A path and its reverse are equivalent.constraint start < finish;solve satisfy; The optional board values describe both the cell identities and the graph boundary. A block contains <>, and the default <> expression gives an out-of-range lookup the same absent value. The occurs tests therefore reject both blocks and positions beyond the board. Only rightward and downward offsets are needed because path treats the edges as undirected. path returns selected edges rather than an ordered cell array. Walking those edges from start to finish recovers the sequence. The native generator constructs that sequence directly, cuts it into the required lengths, may reverse and reorder the pieces, and fills them with words. The published 5×5 instance below shows those three steps directly. 1. Make a path24 open cellsChoose one path through every open cell.2. Cut into slotsCut it into the required word lengths.3. Fill with wordsChoose words and write them along the slots. Those chosen words do not by themselves make a valid puzzle. The same letters may form other dictionary words, and those candidates may admit a second path cover. A trie finds every dictionary word that can be traced without reusing a cell; the second model checks whether those candidate paths have another exact cover. Every cell must occur once, and the selected paths must have the advertised lengths. set of int: OpenCells;set of int: Lengths = 3..10;enum Candidates;array[Candidates] of set of OpenCells: candidate_cells;array[Candidates] of Lengths: candidate_length;array[Lengths] of int: required_count;array[Candidates] of var bool: selected;constraint forall (cell in OpenCells) ( sum (candidate in Candidates where cell in candidate_cells[candidate] ) (selected[candidate]) = 1);constraint forall (length in Lengths) ( sum (candidate in Candidates where candidate_length[candidate] = length ) (selected[candidate]) = required_count[length]);solve satisfy; The Gecode checker stops after finding two covers and accepts only a unique decomposition. Swend’s lexicon starts from SAOL 14 and keeps words supported by the Swedish Kelly list or NyLLex, together with reviewed additions. Wend instead uses a filtered, pinned version of the English Speller Database. Both importers remove palindromes and reversal pairs because a path can be read in either direction. Tracing ONT in Swend Generated boards must contain turns and straight segments, use all four directions, and survive deduplication under rotations and reflections. Within each board size, the generator ranks them by the number of traceable dictionary candidates, followed by Gecode search nodes and failures. The lower, middle, and upper thirds receive the relative labels Easy, Medium, and Hard. Within each third, the generator favours boards with more mirrored letter pairs and a balanced selection of block masks. Hints as small propagation systems# Some of the local deductions used to classify generated puzzles can also explain the next move to a player. Once a puzzle has a known solution, the easiest hint system is still to reveal part of it. I wanted the hint button to make a deduction when the current state supports one, and to be explicit when it falls back to a reveal. Sudoku and Queens have explainable hints backed by a small, puzzle-neutral deduction engine. It knows about exact-one groups, capacity-one groups, conflicts, Hall sets,2 and failed-literal reasoning, which uses the same assumption-propagation-failure test as shaving. It runs rules in teaching order and keeps a shown hint active until its target has been handled. The game adapters give those ideas their concrete meaning: cells and values for Sudoku; rows, columns, regions, and attacks for Queens. Sudoku first reports an incorrect entry. It then tries naked singles, a value with only one place in a row, column, or box, Hall sets of up to four cells,2 and finally a small negative-reasoning step: assume a candidate, propagate forced placements, and reject it if propagation reaches a conflict. Only when none of those rules applies does it reveal a value from the stored solution. Queens follows a similar teaching order. It reports attacking or incorrect queens and a cross that hides a solution square. It marks cells directly attacked by placed queens, finds rows, columns, or regions with one candidate left, and uses locked sets when a collection of regions is confined to the same number of rows or columns. Failed-literal reasoning handles the remaining case by tentatively placing a queen and propagating until two forced queens attack or some group loses its last candidate. The first two examples below are direct deductions. A marks squares that the deduction allows the player to cross out. In the locked-set example, R marks the candidates that justify those actions. Nonogram uses the same line model for solving and for hints, but keeps the hint implementation local. It first reports a marked square that conflicts with the stored picture. Otherwise it enumerates all line patterns compatible with the current marks and the run clues. If every remaining pattern for a row or column agrees on an unknown square, that square is forced. Only when no line has such a deduction does the hint reveal a square from the stored solution. The other games use narrower hint finders. Patches recomputes live rectangle domains, and Tents replays its line, matching, and failed-assumption deductions. Loopy reasons about clue saturation, vertex degree, and premature closed subloops. Zip identifies the first wrong turn or continues the known path, while Wend and Swend progressively reveal a word. When no deduction applies, the hint says that it is revealing part of the stored solution. That keeps the distinction visible: a deduction follows from the current state, while a reveal merely helps the player resume. Summary# Across these games, constraints do three related jobs. They describe valid solutions, detect alternatives during generation, and support deductions for hints. The generators use uniqueness in different ways: Nonogram retains source images that pass a uniqueness check; Sudoku, Loopy, and Patches remove information while preserving a unique answer; Queens, Zip, and Tents repair counterexamples; Wend and Swend reject alternative covers. I started with a large Sudoku corpus and wanted to play a few instances. I ended up with nine playable games (so far). Footnotes# Shaving temporarily assigns a value and propagates to a fixpoint. If that assumption fails, the value can be removed without committing to a branch. Bounds shaving tests the current smallest and largest values of a domain; domain shaving tests every remaining value. I described the corresponding MiniZinc preprocessing modes in the LinkedIn Queens benchmarking post. ↩ Hall’s theorem gives the matching condition behind all_different: any set of k variables must collectively have at least k possible values. If it has exactly k, those values are reserved for those variables and can be removed from every other domain; fewer than k proves failure. Régin’s matching-based propagator uses the general form of this argument to establish domain consistency. Puget’s bounds propagator looks for the cheaper restricted form given by Hall intervals. ↩ ↩2

blocks.html_en: The classification extends the setup in Helmut Simonis’s 2005 paper Sudoku as a Constraint Problem. It tries an ordered family of propagation configurations. Val, Bnd, and Dom refer to value, bounds, and domain propagation; BS and DS add bounds or domain shaving.1 The weakest successful configuration becomes the puzzle’s hardness tag. If none finishes without branching, the tag is Search.

sentences.en: The generator repeats this: whenever possible it adds a numbered checkpoint whose position distinguishes the intended path from the alternative.
sentences.zh: 生成器重复此操作：只要有可能，它就会添加一个编号的检查点，其位置将预期路径与替代路径区分开来。

sentences.en: Sometimes a pair of numbers is needed because the two paths visit those cells in opposite orders.
sentences.zh: 有时需要一对数字，因为两条路径以相反的顺序访问这些单元。

sentences.en: A hedge is added only when numbers cannot separate the counterexample within the clue-density limit.
sentences.zh: 仅当数字无法在线索密度限制内分隔反例时才添加对冲。

blocks.html_en: The process repeats until the intended path is the only solution. Number and hedge limits keep the board from filling with annotations.

sentences.en: The process repeats until the intended path is the only solution.
sentences.zh: 重复该过程，直到预期路径成为唯一的解决方案。

sentences.en: Number and hedge limits keep the board from filling with annotations.
sentences.zh: 数量和对冲限制使董事会无法填写注释。

blocks.html_en: Zip tries the same nine propagation and shaving configurations as Scaling Sudoku, followed by Search when none solves without branching. The interface maps the ten internal tags to relative labels from Gentle through Expert.

sentences.en: Zip tries the same nine propagation and shaving configurations as Scaling Sudoku, followed by Search when none solves without branching.
sentences.zh: Zip 尝试与缩放数独相同的九种传播和剃须配置，然后在没有分支的情况下无法解决问题时进行搜索。

sentences.en: The interface maps the ten internal tags to relative labels from Gentle through Expert.
sentences.zh: 该界面将十个内部标签映射到从 Gentle 到 Expert 的相关标签。

blocks.html_en: Loopy: hide clues from a finished loop#

sentences.en: Loopy: hide clues from a finished loop#
sentences.zh: Loopy：隐藏已完成循环的线索#

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>Most of a 5×5 Loopy loop</figcaption>

sentences.en: Most of a 5×5 Loopy loop
sentences.zh: 5×5 Loopy 循环的大部分

blocks.html_en: Loopy is played on the edges of a square grid. The aim is to draw one closed loop without branches or crossings. A number inside a cell tells how many of its four edges belong to the loop; a blank cell imposes no such count.

sentences.en: Loopy is played on the edges of a square grid.
sentences.zh: Loopy 是在方格的边缘上玩的。

sentences.en: The aim is to draw one closed loop without branches or crossings.
sentences.zh: 目的是绘制一个没有分支或交叉点的闭环。

sentences.en: A number inside a cell tells how many of its four edges belong to the loop; a blank cell imposes no such count.
sentences.zh: 单元格内的数字表示其四个边中有多少条属于循环；空白单元格不强制执行此类计数。

blocks.html_en: The generator begins with the loop. It grows a connected patch of cells while keeping the cells outside the patch connected as well, then rejects any boundary that is not one simple loop. Once that shape is fixed, the generator counts the four surrounding loop edges for every cell and obtains a fully clued puzzle.

sentences.en: The generator begins with the loop.
sentences.zh: 生成器从循环开始。

sentences.en: It grows a connected patch of cells while keeping the cells outside the patch connected as well, then rejects any boundary that is not one simple loop.
sentences.zh: 它会生长出一个相连的细胞块，同时保持块外的细胞也相连，然后拒绝任何不是简单循环的边界。

sentences.en: Once that shape is fixed, the generator counts the four surrounding loop edges for every cell and obtains a fully clued puzzle.
sentences.zh: 一旦形状固定，生成器就会计算每个单元格的四个周围循环边缘，并获得一个完全有线索的谜题。

blocks.html_en: The MiniZinc model assigns one successor variable to each grid vertex. A vertex outside the loop points to itself. The remaining successors form one directed cycle, which is exactly the structure captured by subcircuit. An undirected grid edge belongs to the loop when either endpoint chooses the other as its successor.

sentences.en: The MiniZinc model assigns one successor variable to each grid vertex.
sentences.zh: MiniZinc 模型为每个网格顶点分配一个后继变量。

sentences.en: A vertex outside the loop points to itself.
sentences.zh: 循环外的顶点指向其自身。

sentences.en: The remaining successors form one directed cycle, which is exactly the structure captured by subcircuit.
sentences.zh: 剩余的后继形成一个有向循环，这正是子电路捕获的结构。

sentences.en: An undirected grid edge belongs to the loop when either endpoint chooses the other as its successor.
sentences.zh: 当任一端点选择另一个作为其后继端点时，无向网格边就属于循环。

blocks.html_en: The additional edge constraint rules out a directed two-cycle between adjacent vertices, which would otherwise collapse to a single undirected edge rather than a loop. The output records only in_loop, and the omitted uniqueness loop blocks each discovered edge set. It therefore treats the two directed orientations as the same puzzle solution.

sentences.en: The additional edge constraint rules out a directed two-cycle between adjacent vertices, which would otherwise collapse to a single undirected edge rather than a loop.
sentences.zh: 附加的边约束排除了相邻顶点之间的有向二循环，否则该二循环将崩溃为单个无向边而不是循环。

sentences.en: The output records only in_loop, and the omitted uniqueness loop blocks each discovered edge set.
sentences.zh: 输出仅记录 in_loop，省略的唯一性循环会阻塞每个发现的边集。

sentences.en: It therefore treats the two directed orientations as the same puzzle solution.
sentences.zh: 因此，它将两个定向视为相同的谜题解决方案。

blocks.html_en: The fully clued board is a useful starting point but a poor puzzle. The generator therefore tries hiding clues one at a time. A clue stays hidden only if the intended loop remains unique. For an Easy or Medium candidate, the local deduction engine also keeps the puzzle within the requested band as clues disappear.

sentences.en: The fully clued board is a useful starting point but a poor puzzle.
sentences.zh: 完全有线索的棋盘是一个有用的起点，但却是一个糟糕的谜题。

sentences.en: The generator therefore tries hiding clues one at a time.
sentences.zh: 因此，生成器尝试一次隐藏一个线索。

sentences.en: A clue stays hidden only if the intended loop remains unique.
sentences.zh: 仅当预期循环保持唯一时，线索才会保持隐藏。

sentences.en: For an Easy or Medium candidate, the local deduction engine also keeps the puzzle within the requested band as clues disappear.
sentences.zh: 对于“简单”或“中等”候选者，当线索消失时，本地演绎引擎还会将谜题保持在所请求的范围内。

blocks.html_en: Difficulty is measured by replaying two families of local deductions. A satisfied clue excludes its remaining edges, while a clue that needs every undecided edge forces all of them into the loop. At a grid vertex, two loop edges exclude the other incident edges; one loop edge with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge into the loop; and no selected loop edges with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge out. The bands record how many deduction rounds are needed; every selected puzzle can be completed by these rules without search.

sentences.en: Difficulty is measured by replaying two families of local deductions.
sentences.zh: 难度是通过重播本地扣除的两个系列来衡量的。

sentences.en: A satisfied clue excludes its remaining edges, while a clue that needs every undecided edge forces all of them into the loop.
sentences.zh: 满意的线索会排除其剩余的边缘，而需要每个未确定的边缘的线索会迫使所有边缘进入循环。

sentences.en: At a grid vertex, two loop edges exclude the other incident edges; one loop edge with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge into the loop; and no selected loop edges with only one undecided incident edge forces that edge out.
sentences.zh: 在网格顶点处，两条循环边排除其他入射边；仅具有一个未确定的入射边的一个循环边迫使该边进入循环；并且没有选定的循环边，只有一个未确定的入射边会强制该边向外。

sentences.en: The bands record how many deduction rounds are needed; every selected puzzle can be completed by these rules without search.
sentences.zh: 乐队记录需要多少轮推演；每个选定的谜题都可以通过这些规则完成，无需搜索。

blocks.html_en: Tents: move the trees against an alternative#

sentences.en: Tents: move the trees against an alternative#
sentences.zh: 帐篷：移动树木以对抗替代方案#

blocks.html_en: In Tents, the player places one orthogonally adjacent tent for each tree. No two tents may touch, even diagonally, and the row and column clues give the number of tents in each line. The generator starts from those tents, assigns each one a distinct orthogonally adjacent tree, and derives the counts. Those clues often admit another tent set.

sentences.en: In Tents, the player places one orthogonally adjacent tent for each tree.
sentences.zh: 在帐篷中，玩家为每棵树放置一个正交相邻的帐篷。

sentences.en: No two tents may touch, even diagonally, and the row and column clues give the number of tents in each line.
sentences.zh: 任何两个帐篷都不能接触，即使是对角线也是如此，行和列的线索给出了每行帐篷的数量。

sentences.en: The generator starts from those tents, assigns each one a distinct orthogonally adjacent tree, and derives the counts.
sentences.zh: 生成器从这些帐篷开始，为每个帐篷分配一棵不同的正交相邻树，并导出计数。

sentences.en: Those clues often admit another tent set.
sentences.zh: 这些线索常常允许另一组帐篷的存在。

blocks.html_en: The useful counterexample is the alternative set together with its possible tree matching. When the intended answer is not unique, the generator moves one tree to another square beside its intended tent, choosing a square that prevents the alternative tents from matching every tree. The tent set and line counts stay fixed. The generator recounts solutions after each move and stops when only the intended tent set remains. In the example below, dashed lines show one matching between trees and tents; M marks the moved tree.

sentences.en: The useful counterexample is the alternative set together with its possible tree matching.
sentences.zh: 有用的反例是替代集及其可能的树匹配。

sentences.en: When the intended answer is not unique, the generator moves one tree to another square beside its intended tent, choosing a square that prevents the alternative tents from matching every tree.
sentences.zh: 当预期的答案不唯一时，生成器会将一棵树移动到其预期帐篷旁边的另一个方格，选择一个方格以防止替代帐篷与每棵树匹配。

sentences.en: The tent set and line counts stay fixed.
sentences.zh: 帐篷布景和帐篷数量保持不变。

sentences.en: The generator recounts solutions after each move and stops when only the intended tent set remains.
sentences.zh: 生成器在每次移动后重新计算解决方案，并在只剩下预期的帐篷组时停止。

sentences.en: In the example below, dashed lines show one matching between trees and tents; M marks the moved tree.
sentences.zh: 在下面的示例中，虚线显示了树木和帐篷之间的匹配； M 标记移动的树。

blocks.html_en: The MiniZinc sketch does not need a decision variable for every board cell. A Coordinate record keeps a row and column together, and every tree owns one such decision record for its tent. Whole-array field projections such as tents.row then let global_cardinality count the chosen rows and columns directly. The rest of the listing uses optional lookups at board edges, imaginary 2×2 squares to enforce tent spacing, and sorted output to identify a solution by its tent set rather than a particular tree-to-tent matching.

sentences.en: The MiniZinc sketch does not need a decision variable for every board cell.
sentences.zh: MiniZinc 草图不需要每个板单元的决策变量。

sentences.en: A Coordinate record keeps a row and column together, and every tree owns one such decision record for its tent.
sentences.zh: 坐标记录将行和列保持在一起，每棵树都为其帐篷拥有一个这样的决策记录。

sentences.en: Whole-array field projections such as tents.row then let global_cardinality count the chosen rows and columns directly.
sentences.zh: 整个数组字段投影（例如 tents.row）然后让 global_cardinality 直接计算所选的行和列。

sentences.en: The rest of the listing uses optional lookups at board edges, imaginary 2×2 squares to enforce tent spacing, and sorted output to identify a solution by its tent set rather than a particular tree-to-tent matching.
sentences.zh: 列表的其余部分使用板边缘的可选查找、虚构的 2×2 正方形来强制帐篷间距，以及排序输出以通过其帐篷集而不是特定的树到帐篷匹配来识别解决方案。

blocks.html_en: The parameter array cell_id is only a coordinate lookup. The adjacency constraint uses the same default <> boundary idiom as Zip. Strict equality cannot match the absent value returned outside the board, so the four offsets need no edge cases.

sentences.en: The parameter array cell_id is only a coordinate lookup.
sentences.zh: 参数数组cell_id只是一个坐标查找。

sentences.en: The adjacency constraint uses the same default <> boundary idiom as Zip.
sentences.zh: 邻接约束使用与 Zip 相同的默认 <> 边界习惯用法。

sentences.en: Strict equality cannot match the absent value returned outside the board, so the four offsets need no edge cases.
sentences.zh: 严格相等无法匹配板外返回的缺失值，因此四个偏移量不需要边缘情况。

blocks.html_en: diffn normally keeps rectangles from overlapping. Here each tent is the anchor of an imaginary 2×2 square. Two such squares overlap exactly when their anchor cells coincide or touch along an edge or corner, so one global replaces the eight-neighbour decomposition. It also implies that the tent cells are distinct. The explicit all_different is logically redundant, but it keeps the one-to-one matching visible to a dedicated matching propagator. The imaginary squares may extend past the board; without a container constraint, diffn only constrains them relative to each other.

sentences.en: diffn normally keeps rectangles from overlapping.
sentences.zh: diffn 通常可以防止矩形重叠。

sentences.en: Here each tent is the anchor of an imaginary 2×2 square.
sentences.zh: 这里每个帐篷都是一个假想的 2×2 正方形的锚点。

sentences.en: Two such squares overlap exactly when their anchor cells coincide or touch along an edge or corner, so one global replaces the eight-neighbour decomposition.
sentences.zh: 当两个这样的正方形的锚单元沿着边缘或角重合或接触时，它们恰好重叠，因此一个全局替换了八邻域分解。

sentences.en: It also implies that the tent cells are distinct.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着帐篷单元是不同的。

sentences.en: The explicit all_different is logically redundant, but it keeps the one-to-one matching visible to a dedicated matching propagator.
sentences.zh: 显式的 all_ different 在逻辑上是多余的，但它使一对一匹配对专用匹配传播器可见。

sentences.en: The imaginary squares may extend past the board; without a container constraint, diffn only constrains them relative to each other.
sentences.zh: 假想的方块可以延伸到棋盘之外；如果没有容器约束，diffn 仅约束它们之间的相对关系。

blocks.html_en: The sorted output is deliberate. Since tents is indexed by tree, one tent set can admit several tree-to-tent matchings. The omitted uniqueness loop blocks the sorted cell identifiers, so it counts player-visible tent sets rather than matching witnesses. The native generator uses the same identity when it asks whether a second solution exists.

sentences.en: The sorted output is deliberate.
sentences.zh: 排序的输出是经过深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: Since tents is indexed by tree, one tent set can admit several tree-to-tent matchings.
sentences.zh: 由于帐篷是按树索引的，一组帐篷可以容纳多个树与帐篷的匹配。

sentences.en: The omitted uniqueness loop blocks the sorted cell identifiers, so it counts player-visible tent sets rather than matching witnesses.
sentences.zh: 省略的唯一性循环会阻止排序的单元标识符，因此它会计算玩家可见的帐篷集而不是匹配的见证人。

sentences.en: The native generator uses the same identity when it asks whether a second solution exists.
sentences.zh: 当本机生成器询问是否存在第二个解决方案时，它使用相同的标识。

blocks.html_en: The player-facing Easy, Medium, and Hard labels come from replaying the deterministic deductions used by the hint engine. Easy puzzles need line-count and tent-spacing deductions, grass marks for cells without an adjacent tree, and trees with a single remaining position. Medium puzzles add locked tree sets and one-to-one matching deductions. Hard puzzles require a short failed assumption: try a tent or grass mark, propagate, and reject the assumption when it reaches a contradiction.

sentences.en: The player-facing Easy, Medium, and Hard labels come from replaying the deterministic deductions used by the hint engine.
sentences.zh: 面向玩家的“简单”、“中等”和“困难”标签来自重播提示引擎使用的确定性推论。

sentences.en: Easy puzzles need line-count and tent-spacing deductions, grass marks for cells without an adjacent tree, and trees with a single remaining position.
sentences.zh: 简单的谜题需要扣除行数和帐篷间距、没有相邻树的单元格的草标记以及具有单个剩余位置的树。

sentences.en: Medium puzzles add locked tree sets and one-to-one matching deductions.
sentences.zh: 中型谜题添加锁定树组和一对一匹配推导。

sentences.en: Hard puzzles require a short failed assumption: try a tent or grass mark, propagate, and reject the assumption when it reaches a contradiction.
sentences.zh: 困难的谜题需要一个短暂的失败假设：尝试帐篷或草地标记，传播，并在遇到矛盾时拒绝假设。

blocks.html_en: Empty lines are useful clues, but too many produce striped boards with large inactive areas. The generator therefore sets separate limits on empty rows and empty columns.

sentences.en: Empty lines are useful clues, but too many produce striped boards with large inactive areas.
sentences.zh: 空线是有用的线索，但太多会产生带有大面积非活动区域的条纹板。

sentences.en: The generator therefore sets separate limits on empty rows and empty columns.
sentences.zh: 因此，生成器对空行和空列设置单独的限制。

blocks.html_en: Patches: remove information from a tiling#

sentences.en: Patches: remove information from a tiling#
sentences.zh: 补丁：从平铺中删除信息#

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>Two patches placed on a 5×5 board</figcaption>

sentences.en: Two patches placed on a 5×5 board
sentences.zh: 两个 patch 放置在 5×5 板上

blocks.html_en: Patches asks the player to divide the board into rectangles, one per coloured clue, while respecting any given area or shape. The generator starts from a complete tiling. A bounded depth-first search tiles a square board with rectangles of area at least two, then places one clue in a corner of each rectangle. Initially, every clue gives both the rectangle’s area and its shape: square, wide, or tall.

sentences.en: Patches asks the player to divide the board into rectangles, one per coloured clue, while respecting any given area or shape.
sentences.zh: 补丁要求玩家将棋盘分成矩形，每个颜色的线索一个，同时尊重任何给定的区域或形状。

sentences.en: The generator starts from a complete tiling.
sentences.zh: 生成器从完整的平铺开始。

sentences.en: A bounded depth-first search tiles a square board with rectangles of area at least two, then places one clue in a corner of each rectangle.
sentences.zh: 有界深度优先搜索将一块面积至少为两个矩形的方板平铺，然后在每个矩形的一角放置一条线索。

sentences.en: Initially, every clue gives both the rectangle’s area and its shape: square, wide, or tall.
sentences.zh: 最初，每条线索都给出了矩形的面积和形状：正方形、宽或高。

blocks.html_en: That fully described tiling is usually too easy. The generator shuffles the clue fields and tries removing an area or shape. After every removal, an exact-cover solver counts rectangle tilings up to two; the field stays absent only when the puzzle remains unique.

sentences.en: That fully described tiling is usually too easy.
sentences.zh: 完整描述的平铺通常太容易了。

sentences.en: The generator shuffles the clue fields and tries removing an area or shape.
sentences.zh: 生成器会打乱线索字段并尝试删除区域或形状。

sentences.en: After every removal, an exact-cover solver counts rectangle tilings up to two; the field stays absent only when the puzzle remains unique.
sentences.zh: 每次移除后，精确覆盖解算器都会将矩形平铺计数最多为两个；只有当谜题保持独特时，这个领域才会消失。

blocks.html_en: The corresponding model uses one record for each clue and another for the placement variables of its rectangle. The Boolean covers view is redundant, but it expresses the exact-cover constraint clearly and gives useful propagation from cells back to rectangles. Corner placement is a convention for the generated answer, not a player rule: an alternative rectangle only has to contain its clue.

sentences.en: The corresponding model uses one record for each clue and another for the placement variables of its rectangle.
sentences.zh: 相应的模型对每个线索使用一个记录，对其矩形的放置变量使用另一个记录。

sentences.en: The Boolean covers view is redundant, but it expresses the exact-cover constraint clearly and gives useful propagation from cells back to rectangles.
sentences.zh: 布尔覆盖视图是多余的，但它清楚地表达了精确覆盖约束，并提供了从单元格返回矩形的有用传播。

sentences.en: Corner placement is a convention for the generated answer, not a player rule: an alternative rectangle only has to contain its clue.
sentences.zh: 角的放置是生成答案的约定，而不是玩家规则：替代矩形只需包含其线索。

blocks.html_en: Patches classifies difficulty by giving each clue a domain of candidate rectangles. It uses three custom propagation tiers, named Val, Bnd, and Dom to match the other games. Val removes rectangles that overlap an assigned patch. Bnd also uses cell coverage: if only one clue can still cover a cell, that clue’s domain is restricted accordingly. Dom adds a local support check for the remaining uncovered cells. Bounds- and domain-shaving variants complete the set, followed by Search.

sentences.en: Patches classifies difficulty by giving each clue a domain of candidate rectangles.
sentences.zh: 补丁通过为每个线索提供一个候选矩形域来对难度进行分类。

sentences.en: It uses three custom propagation tiers, named Val, Bnd, and Dom to match the other games.
sentences.zh: 它使用三个自定义传播层（名为 Val、Bnd 和 Dom）来匹配其他游戏。

sentences.en: Val removes rectangles that overlap an assigned patch.
sentences.zh: Val 删除与指定面片重叠的矩形。

sentences.en: Bnd also uses cell coverage: if only one clue can still cover a cell, that clue’s domain is restricted accordingly.
sentences.zh: Bnd还使用小区覆盖：如果只有一条线索仍然可以覆盖一个小区，则该线索的范围将受到相应限制。

sentences.en: Dom adds a local support check for the remaining uncovered cells.
sentences.zh: Dom 添加了对剩余未覆盖单元的本地支持检查。

sentences.en: Bounds- and domain-shaving variants complete the set, followed by Search.
sentences.zh: 边界和域剃须变体完成了该组，其次是搜索。

sentences.en: Wend and Swend: fill a path cover with words#
sentences.zh: Wend 和 Swend：用文字填充路径#

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>Tracing HERBS in Wend</figcaption>

sentences.en: Tracing HERBS in Wend
sentences.zh: 在温德追踪草药

blocks.html_en: Wend and its Swedish sibling Swend ask the player to divide the letter grid into words of the given lengths. Every open cell belongs to one orthogonally connected word path. The two games use the same path and exact-cover models with language-specific word tables.

sentences.en: Wend and its Swedish sibling Swend ask the player to divide the letter grid into words of the given lengths.
sentences.zh: Wend 和它的瑞典兄弟 Swend 要求玩家将字母网格划分为给定长度的单词。

sentences.en: Every open cell belongs to one orthogonally connected word path.
sentences.zh: 每个开放单元都属于一个正交连接的字路径。

sentences.en: The two games use the same path and exact-cover models with language-specific word tables.

blocks.html_en: Sudoku and Queens have explainable hints backed by a small, puzzle-neutral deduction engine. It knows about exact-one groups, capacity-one groups, conflicts, Hall sets,2 and failed-literal reasoning, which uses the same assumption-propagation-failure test as shaving. It runs rules in teaching order and keeps a shown hint active until its target has been handled. The game adapters give those ideas their concrete meaning: cells and values for Sudoku; rows, columns, regions, and attacks for Queens.

blocks.html_en: Sudoku first reports an incorrect entry. Only when none of those rules applies does it reveal a value from the stored solution.

Failed-literal reasoning handles the remaining case by tentatively placing a queen and propagating until two forced queens attack or some group loses its last candidate.

blocks.html_en: Across these games, constraints do three related jobs. They describe valid solutions, detect alternatives during generation, and support deductions for hints. 在我的论文“将数独缩放为约束问题”中，我生成了一个包含 434,201 个数独实例的存储库，大小分别为 6×6 和 36×36 之间的五种。 我在约束编程实验中使用它们来询问哪种传播方案可以在没有分支的情况下解决难题，它如何随大小变化，以及有多少线索将实例从一个硬度类别移动到另一个硬度类别。

我也想玩其中的几个。

那个小小的愿望逐渐向侧面发展。 我现在有 Sudoku、Nonogram、Queens、Zip、Loopy、Tents、Patches、Wend 及其瑞典兄弟 Swend 的可玩版本。 它们收集在游戏页面上。

下面的每个游戏部分都包含一个用 MiniZinc（一种约束建模语言）编写的小模型，并解释了相应生成器的一部分。 这些模型是解释性草图，而不是构建包的程序。 大多数生成和求解代码使用 Gecode 6.4.0。 其他程序可处理导入、光栅化、精确覆盖和包组装。

所有九款游戏的共同点是我从解决方案或源图像开始。 然后，我添加、移动或删除信息，直到预期的答案是唯一的，或者丢弃无法完全修复的候选答案。 一些相同的推论稍后会对难度进行分类并提供提示。

生成和唯一性检查离线进行。 浏览器接收静态谜题和存储的解决方案；它不运行求解器。 难度标签来自传播、搜索或确定性推论测量。 它们在每个包内提供了相对的、机械派生的顺序；他们没有估计玩家会发现谜题有多困难。

使用 MiniZinc 2.10.0 检查列表。 为了让他们保持专注，他们省略了输入验证、搜索注释以及当存在第二个解决方案时拒绝候选者的外循环。 输出被省略，除非它定义了哪些决策构成了谜题解决方案。

数独：从语料库到游戏#

缩放数独语料库以 32,000 个独特可解决的基础谜题开始，尺寸为 6×6、9×9、16×16、25×25 和 36×36。 生成器首先创建一个完整的网格，然后在保留唯一性的同时删除线索。 Gecode 对生成的谜题进行分类。

该分类扩展了 Helmut Simonis 2005 年论文《数独作为约束问题》中的设置。 它尝试一系列有序的传播配置。 Val、Bnd 和 Dom 分别指值、边界和域传播； BS 和 DS 添加边界或域剃须。1 最弱的成功配置成为谜题的硬度标签。 如果没有分支完成，则标记为“搜索”。

基本的数独模型非常简短。 盒子尺寸是数据，它可以让同一模型处理带有 2×3 盒子的 6×6 板和带有 3×3 盒子的常见 9×9 板。

该可玩包是一个可复制的固定种子样本，包含来自固定语料库修订版的 500 个基本谜题，仅限于 6×6 和 9×9 板。 离线导入器将选定的谜题及其已知的解决方案转化为静态包。

让数独看起来更像数独#

生成的谜题不会自动具有人们通常期望从已发布的数独中获得的视觉对称性。 我不想仅仅为了演示而生成一个单独的集合，因此我为选定的谜题编写了离线对称化过程。

有两个有用的自由。 首先，行和列可以以保留盒结构的方式进行排列：带内的行、堆栈内的列以及带和堆栈本身。 其次，缺失的旋转伙伴可以用已知解决方案的值来填充。 后者仅添加信息，因此无法引入第二种解决方案，但根据传播分类器可能会使难题变得更容易。

对于每个谜题，优化器都会枚举从盒子保留布局中获得的不同旋转配对，并根据 180 度旋转对称所需的线索数量对它们进行排名。 它评估三个排名最好的布局，首先尝试完成每个布局的对称性。 如果这改变了硬度标签，它会单独添加合作伙伴线索，并仅保留 Gecode 重现原始标签的添加内容。 最后，它选择具有最少不对称单元的最终布局。

该通道使 500 个谜题中的 228 个完全旋转对称，并将不对称单元总数从 6,172 个减少到 1,928 个。

Nonogram：回到常规#

在 Nonogram 中，玩家填充单元格，以便每行和每列中的运行都与给定的线索匹配。 这个游戏也回溯到我早期的 Gecode 工作。 2005 年，我使用 Gilles Pesant 的正则约束编写了原始的 Gecode nonogram 示例。 它的模型通过正则表达式描述了一条长度为 a, b, ..., z 的线

0* 1^a 0+ 1^b 0+ ... 0+ 1^z 0*

其中 1 是实心方块，0 是空方块。 Gecode 将表达式转换为有限状态机，并约束每一行和每一列遵循它。 Gecode 6.4.0 示例仍然使用相同的紧凑思想。

Jan Wolter 后来将该示例纳入了他对按数字绘制求解器的广泛调查中。 他的评价相当不错：这个小型演示模型与更大的专业求解器一起表现得非常好。

MiniZinc 模型直接构建并应用相同的自动机。 它的运行线索是列表，因此行和列可以包含不同数量的运行而无需填充。 函数 line_regexp 从每个列表构建正则表达式字符串。 MiniZinc 将该字符串编译为有限状态机，并常规地将其应用于行或列。

较新的图标包从固定的 Heroicons 2.2.0 和 Phosphor Icons 2.1.1 档案中的 SVG 开始。 离线光栅化器以高分辨率渲染每个图标，将其适合四种板尺寸之一，并将结果阈值分为填充和空单元格。

每个源图标都分配给一种板尺寸，因此同一图像无法以多种分辨率重新出现。 选择器会拒绝具有极端填充率、过多连接组件、重复指纹或不平衡线索的栅格，然后优先选择经过审查的或更详细的轮廓。 导入的位图必须满足导出的线索，并且 Gecode 必须找不到第二个解决方案。

确定性重放记录初始行模糊度和最大初始候选集，然后测量推论轮次和未解析的单元格。 与 Gecode 的搜索节点和失败一起，这些测量结果对每个大小内的有效实例进行排名。

皇后区：围绕解决方案扩展区域#

皇后是星球大战的一星形式：在每一行、每列和彩色区域放置一个皇后，并且两个皇​​后不能接触。 生成器从有效的非接触皇后排列开始，并从每个皇后中生长一个正交连接的区域。 然后，它会沿着区域边界扰乱非皇后单元，同时保持连接性。

下面的小示例从基本解决方案开始，然后显示围绕其生长的建议区域边界。 第二个解决方案对于这些边界是有效的，从而使其成为无效的谜题实例。 将标记为 M 的单元移动到邻近区域会消除这种替代方案，因此一次边界单元移动使预期的解决方案独一无二。 真实的生成器会重复这种更改，同时检查区域连通性并将每个解决方案计数停止为 2。

对于拼图模型来说，每行一个变量就足够了。 它的价值就是女王的专栏。 不同的列处理列规则，而在每个皇后位置索引区域矩阵一次处理所有彩色区域。

区域重新标记以及方板的八次旋转和反射被简化为一个规范指纹，从而防止同一谜题的伪装副本。 生成器还限制了微小的和占主导地位的区域；我在衡量了已发布的 LinkedIn Queens 董事会后选择了这些限制。 难度使用与缩放数独相同的传播和剃须配置，当没有人在没有分支的情况下解决棋盘时，其次是搜索。

zip: 求一个反例#

在《Zip》中，玩家在每个单元格中绘制一条路径，同时按顺序访问编号的线索并避开树篱。 生成器将路径表示为 Gecode 电路：每个板单元都有一个后继单元，并且一个额外的返回节点将最终线索连接回线索 1。 电路约束排除了断开的子路线，而反向路径和位置视图使编号排序约束变得明确。

该模型表示具有行和列偏移的正交运动。 对于每个单元格，它都会尝试四个方向。 MiniZinc 的默认 <> 将越界查找转换为不存在的单元格；由于缺席的单元格不能等于后继单元格，因此棋盘外的方向从析取中消失。 这避免了单独的邻接矩阵。

为了决定显示哪些数字和树篱，Zip 生成器仅从第一个和最后一个数字开始。 它要求求解器提供第二条路径，然后研究该反例。 下面的示例在添加一个检查点后开始。 两条路径均遵循可见线索 1、2 和 3。

添加的线索表明，左中单元格必须出现在中上单元格之后。 对于预期路径来说是这样，但反例则不然，因此一种歧义消失了。 生成器重复此操作：只要有可能，它就会添加一个编号的检查点，其位置将预期路径与替代路径区分开来。 有时需要一对数字，因为两条路径以相反的顺序访问这些单元。 仅当数字无法在线索密度限制内分隔反例时才添加对冲。

重复该过程，直到预期路径成为唯一的解决方案。 数量和对冲限制使董事会无法填写注释。

Zip 尝试与缩放数独相同的九种传播和剃须配置，然后在没有分支的情况下无法解决问题时进行搜索。 该界面将十个内部标签映射到从 Gentle 到 Expert 的相关标签。

Loopy：隐藏已完成循环的线索#

Loopy 是在方格的边缘上玩的。 目的是绘制一个没有分支或交叉点的闭环。 单元格内的数字表示其四个边中有多少条属于循环；空白单元格不强制执行此类计数。

生成器从循环开始。 它会生长出一个相连的细胞块，同时保持块外的细胞也相连，然后拒绝任何不是简单循环的边界。 一旦形状固定，生成器就会计算每个单元格的四个周围循环边缘，并获得一个完全有线索的谜题。

MiniZinc 模型为每个网格顶点分配一个后继变量。 循环外的顶点指向其自身。 剩余的后继形成一个有向循环，这正是子电路捕获的结构。 当任一端点选择另一个作为其后继端点时，无向网格边就属于循环。

附加的边约束排除了相邻顶点之间的有向二循环，否则该二循环将崩溃为单个无向边而不是循环。 输出仅记录 in_loop，省略的唯一性循环会阻塞每个发现的边集。 因此，它将两个定向视为相同的谜题解决方案。

完全有线索的棋盘是一个有用的起点，但却是一个糟糕的谜题。 因此，生成器尝试一次隐藏一个线索。 仅当预期循环保持唯一时，线索才会保持隐藏。 对于“简单”或“中等”候选者，当线索消失时，本地演绎引擎还会将谜题保持在所请求的范围内。

难度是通过重播本地扣除的两个系列来衡量的。 满意的线索会排除其剩余的边缘，而需要每个未确定的边缘的线索会迫使所有边缘进入循环。 在网格顶点处，两条循环边排除其他入射边；仅具有一个未确定的入射边的一个循环边迫使该边进入循环；并且没有选定的循环边，只有一个未确定的入射边会强制该边向外。 乐队记录需要多少轮推演；每个选定的谜题都可以通过这些规则完成，无需搜索。

帐篷：移动树木以对抗替代方案#

在帐篷中，玩家为每棵树放置一个正交相邻的帐篷。 任何两个帐篷都不能接触，即使是对角线也是如此，行和列的线索给出了每行帐篷的数量。 生成器从这些帐篷开始，为每个帐篷分配一棵不同的正交相邻树，并导出计数。 这些线索常常允许另一组帐篷的存在。

有用的反例是替代集及其可能的树匹配。 当预期的答案不唯一时，生成器会将一棵树移动到其预期帐篷旁边的另一个方格，选择一个方格以防止替代帐篷与每棵树匹配。 帐篷布景和帐篷数量保持不变。 生成器在每次移动后重新计算解决方案，并在只剩下预期的帐篷组时停止。 在下面的示例中，虚线显示了树木和帐篷之间的匹配； M 标记移动的树。

MiniZinc 草图不需要每个板单元的决策变量。 坐标记录将行和列保持在一起，每棵树都为其帐篷拥有一个这样的决策记录。 整个数组字段投影（例如 tents.row）然后让 global_cardinality 直接计算所选的行和列。 列表的其余部分使用板边缘的可选查找、虚构的 2×2 正方形来强制帐篷间距，以及排序输出以通过其帐篷集而不是特定的树到帐篷匹配来识别解决方案。

参数数组cell_id只是一个坐标查找。 邻接约束使用与 Zip 相同的默认 <> 边界习惯用法。 严格相等无法匹配板外返回的缺失值，因此四个偏移量不需要边缘情况。

diffn 通常可以防止矩形重叠。 这里每个帐篷都是一个假想的 2×2 正方形的锚点。 当两个这样的正方形的锚单元沿着边缘或角重合或接触时，它们恰好重叠，因此一个全局替换了八邻域分解。 这也意味着帐篷单元是不同的。 显式的 all_ different 在逻辑上是多余的，但它使一对一匹配对专用匹配传播器可见。 假想的方块可以延伸到棋盘之外；如果没有容器约束，diffn 仅约束它们之间的相对关系。

排序的输出是经过深思熟虑的。 由于帐篷是按树索引的，一组帐篷可以容纳多个树与帐篷的匹配。 省略的唯一性循环会阻止排序的单元标识符，因此它会计算玩家可见的帐篷集而不是匹配的见证人。 当本机生成器询问是否存在第二个解决方案时，它使用相同的标识。

面向玩家的“简单”、“中等”和“困难”标签来自重播提示引擎使用的确定性推论。 简单的谜题需要扣除行数和帐篷间距、没有相邻树的单元格的草标记以及具有单个剩余位置的树。 中型谜题添加锁定树组和一对一匹配推导。 困难的谜题需要一个短暂的失败假设：尝试帐篷或草地标记，传播，并在遇到矛盾时拒绝假设。

空线是有用的线索，但太多会产生带有大面积非活动区域的条纹板。 因此，生成器对空行和空列设置单独的限制。

补丁：从平铺中删除信息#

补丁要求玩家将棋盘分成矩形，每个颜色的线索一个，同时尊重任何给定的区域或形状。 生成器从完整的平铺开始。 有界深度优先搜索将一块面积至少为两个矩形的方板平铺，然后在每个矩形的一角放置一条线索。 最初，每条线索都给出了矩形的面积和形状：正方形、宽或高。

完整描述的平铺通常太容易了。 生成器会打乱线索字段并尝试删除区域或形状。 每次移除后，精确覆盖解算器都会将矩形平铺计数最多为两个；只有当谜题保持独特时，这个领域才会消失。

相应的模型对每个线索使用一个记录，对其矩形的放置变量使用另一个记录。 布尔覆盖视图是多余的，但它清楚地表达了精确覆盖约束，并提供了从单元格返回矩形的有用传播。 角的放置是生成答案的约定，而不是玩家规则：替代矩形只需包含其线索。

补丁通过为每个线索提供一个候选矩形域来对难度进行分类。 它使用三个自定义传播层（名为 Val、Bnd 和 Dom）来匹配其他游戏。 Val 删除与指定面片重叠的矩形。 Bnd还使用小区覆盖：如果只有一条线索仍然可以覆盖一个小区，则该线索的范围将受到相应限制。 Dom 添加了对剩余未覆盖单元的本地支持检查。 边界和域剃须变体完成了该组，其次是搜索。

Wend 和 Swend：用文字填充路径#

Wend 和它的瑞典兄弟 Swend 要求玩家将字母网格划分为给定长度的单词。 每个开放单元都属于一个正交连接的字路径。 这两款游戏使用相同的路径和精确覆盖模型以及特定于语言的单词表。

一代人向后运行这个过程。 它选择一个对称的块掩码和一条穿过每个开放单元的路径，将路径切割成三到十之间的长度，并用单词填充这些片段。

第一个 MiniZinc 草图直接对生成的几何部分进行建模。 开放单元格是无向网格图中的节点。 要求 MiniZinc 的路径约束包括每个开放节点，给出从开始到结束的一条哈密顿路径。

可选的板值描述了单元格标识和图形边界。 块包含 <>，默认的 <> 表达式会为超出范围的查找提供相同的缺失值。 因此，所发生的测试会拒绝棋盘之外的区块和位置。 仅需要向右和向下偏移，因为路径将边缘视为无向。

路径返回选定的边而不是有序元胞数组。 从开始到结束遍历这些边缘可以恢复序列。 本机生成器直接构造该序列，将其切割成所需的长度，可以反转和重新排序这些片段，并用单词填充它们。

Gecode 检查器在找到两个封面后停止并仅接受唯一的分解。

Swend 的词典从 SAOL 14 开始，保留瑞典凯利列表或 NyLLex 支持的单词以及经过审核的添加内容。 Wend 相反使用经过过滤、固定的英语拼写数据库版本。 两个导入器都会删除回文和反转对，因为可以在任一方向读取路径。

生成的板必须包含转弯和直线段，使用所有四个方向，并在旋转和反射下进行重复数据删除。 在每个板尺寸内，生成器根据可追踪字典候选的数量对它们进行排名，然后是 Gecode 搜索节点和失败。 下、中、上三分之一的部分分别带有简单、中等和困难的相对标签。 在每三分之一内，生成器倾向于具有更多镜像字母对和均衡选择的块掩码的板。

作为小型传播系统的提示#

一些用于对生成的谜题进行分类的局部推论也可以向玩家解释下一步行动。 一旦谜题有了已知的解决方案，最简单的提示系统仍然是揭示其中的一部分。 我希望提示按钮在当前状态支持时进行推论，并在回退到显示时明确显示。

数独和皇后有可解释的提示，由小型、谜题中立的推演引擎支持。 它知道精确一组、容量一组、冲突、霍尔集2和失败的文字推理，它使用与剃须相同的假设传播失败测试。 它按照教学顺序运行规则，并保持显示的提示处于活动状态，直到其目标被处理为止。 游戏适配器赋予这些想法具体的含义：数独的单元格和值；皇后区的行、列、区域和攻击。

数独首先报告错误的输入。 然后，它尝试裸单，即行、列或框中只有一个位置的值，最多包含四个单元格的霍尔集2，最后是一个小的否定推理步骤：假设一个候选者，传播强制放置，如果传播发生冲突则拒绝它。 只有当这些规则都不适用时，它才会显示存储解决方案中的值。

皇后区遵循类似的教学顺序。 它报告攻击或不正确的皇后以及隐藏解方格的十字。 它标记被放置的皇后直接攻击的单元格，查找剩下一个候选的行、列或区域，并在区域集合仅限于相同数量的行或列时使用锁定集。 失败的字面推理通过暂时放置皇后并传播直到两个被迫皇后攻击或某个群体失去最后一个候选人来处理剩余的情况。

下面的前两个例子是直接演绎。 A 标记方格表示扣除项允许玩家划掉。 在锁定集示例中，R 标记了证明这些操作合理的候选者。

Nonogram 使用相同的线模型进行求解和提示，但将提示实现保留在本地。 它首先报告一个与存储的图片冲突的标记方块。 否则，它会枚举与当前标记和运行线索兼容的所有线条图案。 如果行或列的每个剩余模式都与未知方格一致，则该方格被强制。 仅当没有行具有此类推导时，提示才会显示存储解决方案中的正方形。

其他游戏使用较窄的提示查找器。 补丁重新计算实时矩形域，帐篷重播其线、匹配和失败的假设推论。 关于线索饱和度、顶点度数和过早闭合子循环的荒谬原因。 Zip 识别第一个错误的转弯或继续已知的路径，而 Wend 和 Swend 逐渐显示一个单词。 当不适用扣除时，提示表示它正在显示存储的解决方案的一部分。

这使得区别显而易见：根据当前状态进行扣除，而显示仅帮助玩家恢复。

概括＃

在这些游戏中，约束起着三项相关的作用。 它们描述有效的解决方案，在生成过程中检测替代方案，并支持提示的推论。 生成器以不同的方式使用唯一性：Nonogram 保留通过唯一性检查的源图像；数独、循环和补丁会删除信息，同时保留唯一的答案； Queens、Zip 和 Tents 修复反例； Wend 和 Swend 拒绝替代封面。

我从一个大型数独语料库开始，想玩几个实例。 我最终完成了九个可玩的游戏（到目前为止）。
